summary: Dry Tortugas Light on Loggerhead Key, a brick tower first lit in 1858 and automated in 1987; the keepers' roster runs 1858 to the 1980s.

lens.note: first order Fresnel, 1858; second-order bivalve from 1909; current VRB-25 (USLHS)

structures.note: Putnam (1917) gives 157 ft; USLHS gives 150.67 ft above mean high water for the light; LighthouseFriends says the 1856 plan was for a 150-ft tower.

access.note: Owned by the National Park Service. Reached by seaplane or ferry to Garden Key; landing on Loggerhead Key needs your own boat or a park-permitted guide (LighthouseFriends). USLHS lists it as open to the public.

visit.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends). The pier at Loggerhead Key is closed to the public.

stay.note: LighthouseFriends: volunteers stay in the original building; check with the host organisation for dates and requirements.

events.note: Congress appropriated $35,000 on 18 August 1856 for a second, more powerful light on Loggerhead Key
Brick conical tower on Loggerhead Key; supervised by Captain Daniel P. Woodbury
First illuminated 1 July 1858
First-order Fresnel lens by L. Sautter & Company of Paris
Attempt on head keeper Benjamin H. Kerr's life, as LighthouseFriends describes an 1860 report by G. Phillips
Hurricane of 1873 inflicted heavy damage on the Loggerhead Key tower
Upper tower masonry rebuilt after $75,000 appropriated on 3 March 1875
Red sector added on 30 April 1893 for a reef off the tower
Tower ironwork scraped and painted, new storm doors
Second-order bivalve lens purchased by the Lighthouse Board
17 March: keepers E. J. Russell, B. M. [Holton M.] Roberts and C. Johnson brought the captain and crew of the wrecked schooner Pendleton Brothers to the station
Storm of July 1916 destroyed the old wharf
8 May: keeper Charles Johnson and assistant Robert J. Fine went to a fishing schooner ashore on rocks near Bird Key
Keeper's dwelling (one-story brick bungalow) built 1922-1923 at a cost of $6,498
2 November 1923: second assistant C. C. Turner assisted a disabled vessel that later sank (reported in the Bulletin of 1 January 1924)
Radiobeacon established on 21 December 1927; the first in Florida
Generators installed in a frame addition to the former oil house to power the light
Two-story keepers' dwelling burned and was razed
Mercury float damaged; revolving lens stopped; later replaced with a DCB-24 and then a VRB-25
Lighthouse automated
Dry Tortugas National Park created

corrections.why: The 1826 light stood on Garden Key (Putnam 1917; LighthouseFriends). The Loggerhead Key tower was built and first lit in 1858 (USLHS, LighthouseFriends). The USLHS place record's 'Year Established: 1826' seems to carry the Garden Key date.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1826 (USLHS) and 1858 (Wikidata, Rowlett) differ because the 1826 light stood on Garden Key, about three miles east (Putnam 1917; LighthouseFriends). The Loggerhead Key tower dates from 1858 (USLHS 'Year Tower Established: 1858'; LighthouseFriends 'first illuminated on July 1, 1858').

Putnam (1917) gives 157 feet for the tower; the USLHS record gives 150.67 feet above mean high water for the light; LighthouseFriends describes a 150-foot tower in the 1856 plan. Different measures of the same tower.

notes_for_editor: Keepers: every line is from the USLHS roster printed by roster.py (154 lines, 1858-1985) with the archive's person slug on each line. Names in the 1913 and 1919 Bulletin items: the 1913 Bulletin reads 'B . M. Roberts' in the OCR; the 1912-1917 index gives 'Roberts, Holton M., asst keeper Dry Tortugas'; the roster lists Holton M. Roberts as first assistant 1911-1917. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1913 first assistant is named Holton M. Roberts from the 1912-1917 index (index PDF p.38, source 14) and the USLHS roster, not by column position; the Bulletin text (PDF p.24) reads B. M. Roberts. The 1924 Turner item sits in the Bulletin of 1 January 1924 (PDF p.6) and reports 2 November 1923, so the event year is corrected from 1924 to 1923. The 1919 Bulletin text (PDF p.30) names Charles Johnson, keeper, and Robert J. Fine, assistant keeper. The copper-screen point is from the 1923 Bulletin (PDF p.40, source 10). The 1913 Bulletin names 'E. J. Russell, keeper' (the index gives 'Russell, E.J., keeper Dry Tortugas, rescue'). The 1919 schooner's name is illegible in the OCR ('GltlT1/'), so it is not given in the story. The 1860 attempt on Kerr's life rests on LighthouseFriends' account of an 1860 report by G. Phillips; the report itself was not read. Turtle-hunt account is LighthouseFriends' quotation of an officer's wife, whose original record was not read. The Loggerhead Key tower height: Putnam's 157 ft against the USLHS 150.67 ft above MHW; not reconciled. Access: USLHS says 'Open to Public: Yes'; LighthouseFriends says grounds open, tower closed, landing by permit or guide. The 1912 fire at the Tortugas Harbor light (Garden Key) is a different station and is not in this story. Post-1960 Coast Guard keepers appear only in the roster, as published; they are not named in the prose. No NRHP nomination was checked for this station. Bulletin and commissioner page numbers are PDF/scan pages; printed numbers not confirmed.
